cells.tense: The imagining is complete and the feeling of it has arrived in full.
cells.ask: Let something end this week and don't replace it. Leave the space open for a day and notice what's still there.
cells.core:
You can let a thing finish and feel good about it, which is rarer than it sounds. The ending happened, you stayed in it while it happened, and what you'd pictured came all the way through to being felt. That's why it sits well. Nothing is being avoided here, and nothing is being forced.

Direction comes from real engagement, not pressure. What you pick up next, you pick up because you want it, and it moves at its own pace. You don't have to manufacture momentum. The spot where the old thing was isn't empty in a bad way. It's open, and staying open for a while is the whole work.
cells.sheetLine: An ending did its work, and you're letting it be done.
cells.verb: Feeling what was imagined until it is fully satisfied
cells.place: In the clearing that has to finish before the next thing can start

cells.tense: You're gripping the next thing before the current ending has finished.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been postponing closure on and close it today, then leave the day after empty.
cells.core:
There's a clean version of this and you know it. You finish a thing, the finish holds, and you don't rush toward what comes next because what comes next will still be there. Your care is steady — you tend what's growing without squeezing it, and you hold a space without white-knuckling what it turns into.

Instead you're reaching into the next thing before this one is done. You're managing a future that hasn't arrived, and the managing is eating satisfaction that was already yours. What you're tending doesn't need gripping. Let one thing actually end without a plan for the next one already in your hand. The ending isn't a loss. It's what gives the next thing a floor to stand on.

cells.tense: The ending happened and you're still standing at the door behind you.
cells.ask: Write one plain sentence about what actually ended, no more than that, and read it once out loud.
cells.core:
You can recognize a thing is over and admit it to yourself. You sit with what you know before you announce it, and it lands without needing an argument. That's how something gets to be well lived and fully finished both — the satisfaction has room because you let the over be over.

The ending is behind you and you're still at the door. The clearing is there and you haven't walked into it. You don't need more imagining. You need the quiet step of naming one true thing, letting your mind hold it before you say anything about it. The space is still open. You just haven't stepped in.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the door after the ending already happened.
cells.verb: Feeling what was imagined until it is fully satisfied

cells.tense: You're already clearing what needs to go and calling it something else.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've already let go of, out loud and plainly, and don't argue for why it had to go.
cells.core:
You notice what's finished and you let it finish. You sort what matters from what doesn't, and you do it quietly and steadily. Time alone helps instead of cutting you off. The refining serves what's growing rather than feeding worry.

That work is already underway. Things have ended around you and you've moved through them. But when you talk about it, it sounds like the circumstances made that call. You're the one who let them go. What you call the situation is your own clear seeing at work. Say the ending was yours, and the satisfaction has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You're already clearing the way, though you haven't said so.
